keySentence: The biggest waste of time is doing nothing — even a wrong road leads somewhere new.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: Milo made many mistakes during his long journey through the Lands Beyond. He took wrong roads and ended up in strange and unexpected places along the way. But every wrong road taught him something he would not have learned by going the right way. The worst part of his journey was not any mistake but the time he spent doing absolutely nothing. In the Doldrums he wasted time without learning anything at all and that felt the worst of everything. Milo decided that moving forward, even in the wrong direction, was always better than standing still. The biggest waste of time is doing nothing — even a wrong road leads somewhere new.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: By the time Milo reached the Castle in the Air he had a long list of mistakes and wrong turns behind him. He had jumped to conclusions, lingered in the Doldrums, and followed bad advice from unreliable characters. But looking back he could see that each mistake had given him something that he now genuinely needed. The time in the Doldrums had taught him how precious time was and how easily it could be wasted without noticing. The Island of Conclusions had taught him what happened when he moved without thinking about where he was going. Even the longest detours had introduced him to characters who gave him tools and ideas he used in the final battle. The one thing he had gained nothing from was the time he had spent standing still and doing nothing at all. The biggest waste of time is doing nothing — even a wrong road leads somewhere new.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: Milo's journey through the Lands Beyond functions as an extended meditation on the relationship between action and learning. The story's consistent position is that engagement — even imperfect, misdirected, or confused engagement — produces growth. Non-engagement, by contrast, produces nothing and costs everything in terms of the time that passes without being used. This position is more radical than it first appears because it includes wrong turns in the category of productive action. A wrong turn produces frustration, surprise, and new information — all of which are raw material for understanding. The Doldrums produce none of these things and are therefore the one place in the Lands Beyond that offers no return at all. Milo leaves every other location changed in some way — he leaves the Doldrums unchanged, only diminished by the time spent. Juster's final lesson is not that you should never make mistakes but that you should never mistake stillness for safety. The biggest waste of time is doing nothing — even a wrong road leads somewhere new.
